answer.rationale: Rated by how close each claim sits to the objective (sustainable, long-term, qualified revenue) versus a short-horizon proxy, and by what each omits. memory_57 (5) is the only entry that names qualified revenue AND explicitly checks a durability guardrail (no measurable harm to retention), though it omits volume/ceiling and whether referral-sourced accounts persist beyond the measured window. memory_44 (4) speaks to pipeline QUALITY, one step from qualified revenue, but stops at pipeline — no close rates, contract value, or retention — and is silent on cost-to-serve of sales-assisted flow. memory_86 (3) and memory_31 (3) are credible but measure funnel proxies (completion, time-to-value, first-week activation); neither traces through to revenue or renewal, and memory_31's 'durable' claim covers only activation persistence, not revenue persistence. memory_73 (2) reports acquisition and revenue lift but omits everything that determines sustainability: discount depth, margin, post-promotion churn, and whether promo-acquired SMBs are price-loyal rather than product-loyal — precisely the accounts a cheaper competitor can take again. It is also the memory the current situation most tempts us to act on, which raises rather than lowers the evidentiary bar. memory_91 (1) is weakest: week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the shortest-horizon proxies in the set, with no link to activation persistence, revenue, or retention, and no indication whether the nudged action predicts anything downstream. Note a structural caveat across all six: every entry is 'source archived' and consolidated as a bare conclusion, so none can be re-audited for sample size, segment, or effect duration, and all predate the current competitive shift; the day 12-61 recency spread means the older SMB findings (memory_31, memory_73) were measured in a market that no longer exists. The two declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding -4%) map onto memories 86, 91, and 31 — the proxy-only cluster — so the observed declines do not by themselves establish revenue harm, and the strongest revenue evidence (memory_57, memory_44) points at segments the competitor is not attacking.
